TASK: stop the CI 'Fast feedback' job from running heavy test files because tests/shard_durations.json is stale.

BACKGROUND: scripts/quick_suite.py skips any test file whose recorded time in tests/shard_durations.json is >= 15 s, but a file MISSING from that json counts as 0 s and is always run. The json was last regenerated on 2026-10-24 and lists 198 files; the repo now has ~310 tests/test_*.py files. The 68 unlisted files cost ~236 s of the quick tier's ~425 s, and several are heavy (tests/test_live_baseline_enforce.py ~24 s, tests/test_environment_screen.py ~23 s, tests/test_drain_details_prose_probe.py ~23 s, tests/test_journey_prefix_equivalence.py ~18 s, tests/test_hidden_bench_arm_probe.py ~16 s). tests/test_spine_expected_reveals.py is listed at 2.3 s but now takes ~15 s. The same json also drives CI shard balancing (tests/conftest.py assign_test_nodes_to_shards; tests/test_shard_balance.py). The json format is {"version": 1, "files": {"tests/test_x.py": seconds, ...}}. Running pytest with `--tier-report PATH` (tests/conftest.py pytest_sessionfinish) already writes a JSON report whose `file_seconds` key maps each test file to its summed setup+call+teardown seconds, rounded to 2 decimals - reuse it, do not re-implement timing.

OWNED FILES (edit nothing else): scripts/regen_shard_durations.py (new), scripts/quick_suite.py, tests/shard_durations.json, tests/test_regen_shard_durations.py (new), tests/test_quick_suite.py, docs/testing-runbook.md (add or edit at most two short lines next to the existing quick_suite / shard lines; keep the runbook short; no counts, dates or results).

   - default: run the FULL suite once as `<sys.executable> -m pytest -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider -n 4 --tier-report <temp file>` from the repo root with TMPDIR defaulting to /tmp, then write tests/shard_durations.json from the report's file_seconds (version 1, keys sorted, 2-decimal floats, trailing newline, same indent style as the current file). Refuse to write (exit nonzero, say why) if pytest's exit status is not 0 or 5.
   - `--missing-only`: run only the test files that exist on disk but are absent from the json, merge their times into the existing entries, and drop entries for files that no longer exist. With nothing missing, say so and exit 0 without running pytest.
   - `--from-report PATH`: skip running pytest and build from an existing tier report (combined with --missing-only it merges only the missing files). This is what the unit tests exercise.
   - Keep the pure parts (which files are missing/stale, building/merging the payload) as plain functions with a durations-path parameter, like quick_suite.py does.
2. scripts/quick_suite.py: when selected files are missing from the json, print one warning after the run (and in --list output) naming how many and listing them, plus the fix command `uv run python scripts/regen_shard_durations.py --missing-only`. Do not change selection behaviour or the threshold.
3. tests/test_regen_shard_durations.py (fast, hermetic, mark like neighbouring script tests so it runs in the CI fast-feedback tier `-m "(unit or component) and not authoring_quality"`): (a) building from a fake report writes the expected sorted json; (b) --missing-only merge keeps existing entries, adds missing ones, drops stale ones; (c) the real repo check: every tests/**/test_*.py file on disk has an entry in the real tests/shard_durations.json and every entry names an existing file - its failure message must list the offending files and the fix command. Extend tests/test_quick_suite.py for the new warning.
4. Regenerate the real tests/shard_durations.json with the default full run of your new script (PYTHONPATH=$PWD, the main .venv python as above; machine should be otherwise idle). If the full run has failing tests, report them in notes and still do not hand-edit the json - use --from-report on the report from a run that passed.
5. Run `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/quick_suite.py --list` before and after and put both SKIPPED lists and the predicted CPU seconds in the notes. Run tests/test_shard_balance.py, tests/test_quick_suite.py and tests/test_regen_shard_durations.py; all must pass with the new json.
